title: The finite-type neutral component of a locally finite type group over an arbitrary field
statement:
Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field], and let $G$ be a group scheme over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Write $e\in |G|$ for the point of its identity section, and let $C$ be the connected component of $e$, meaning the maximal connected subset containing $e$ [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Then $C$ is open and closed in $|G|$. With the open-subscheme structure, $G^0=C$ is a subgroup scheme of $G$ [def-weil-open-immersion], is of finite type over $k$, and is geometrically irreducible (after every field extension its underlying space is nonempty and irreducible) [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. For every field extension $K/k$, the open subschemes of $G_K$ satisfy
$$(G^0)_K=(G_K)^0,$$
where base change is as in [def-pc-base-change] and the component on the right contains the base-changed identity. Neither quasi-compactness of $G$, perfectness of $k$, nor smoothness, reducedness or commutativity of $G$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0B7R, proposition-connected-component: canonical quasi-compact geometrically irreducible identity subgroup for any field. Openness in the locally finite type case: topology.tex Tags 04MF (lemma-locally-Noetherian-locally-connected) and 04ME (lemma-locally-connected), with local Noetherianity over a field. Field-extension equality is the component characterization applied to its geometrically connected clopen subgroup.

proof.text: A field is Noetherian: its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian by pqf-def-locnoeth. Apply pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft to $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, which is locally of finite type by hypothesis, to obtain local Noetherianity of $G$. Consequently lem-sc-locnoeth-components-locally-finite makes the irreducible components of $G$ locally finite; no quasi-compactness of $G$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0B7R, locally finite type specialization; Morphisms Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), Topology Tag 0052 (lemma-Noetherian).

proof.text: Distinct irreducible components of $G$ are disjoint. Indeed, fix $x\in G$ and an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing it, with corresponding prime $\mathfrak p$. The local ring $A_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_{G,x}$ has a unique minimal prime by lem-sfb-group-local-minimal-prime. The inclusion-preserving prime correspondence in lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization identifies its minimal primes with the minimal primes of $A$ contained in $\mathfrak p$: any prime strictly below such a prime is still contained in $\mathfrak p$, so minimality is preserved both ways. By lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes, exactly one irreducible component of $U$ contains $x$. The injectivity of intersection with $U$ from lem-sc-components-open-injection implies that at most one irreducible component of $G$ contains $x$. Every point belongs to one by lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover. Hence exactly one does.

source.place: Tag 047M (lemma-group-scheme-field-geometrically-irreducible), part (1); affine component description (Algebra Tag 00ES) and localization correspondence (Algebra Tag 00E3).

proof.text: Let $Z$ be the unique irreducible component containing $e$, supplied by lem-sfb-group-local-minimal-prime. It is closed by def-weil-irreducible-components. At any $z\in Z$, choose an open neighbourhood $V$ meeting only finitely many irreducible components, by step 1. Remove from $V$ every component in this finite list other than $Z$. Step 2 shows that none contains $z$; closedness of components shows that the result is an open neighbourhood of $z$. Since components cover $G$ by lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover, this neighbourhood is contained in $Z$. Thus $Z$ is open and closed. Irreducibility implies connectedness directly: a nontrivial clopen separation would express $Z$ as the union of two proper closed subsets. Hence $Z\subseteq C$ by maximality of $C$. Connectedness of $C$ prevents it from meeting both $Z$ and its clopen complement. Since $e\in Z$, we obtain $C=Z$. Give $C$ its open-subscheme structure. Its reduction has exactly the reduced induced structure on $Z$: both sheaves are obtained by restricting $\mathcal O_G$ to the open subset $Z$ and quotienting by the nilradical. By lem-sfb-group-local-minimal-prime this reduced scheme is geometrically irreducible. By lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism its map to $C$ remains a homeomorphism after every field extension. Therefore $C$ itself is geometrically irreducible, including its original nilpotent structure.

source.place: Tag 047M, parts (2)-(3); Tag 0B7R, identification of the neutral component. Schemes Tag 01J4 (reduction); Morphisms Tag 054M (reduction-universal-homeomorphism).

proof.text: By lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product (with $U=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $V=W=C$), $C\times_kC$ is the open subscheme $\mathrm{pr}_1^{-1}(C)\cap\mathrm{pr}_2^{-1}(C)$ of $G\times_kG$, so multiplication restricts to it; likewise $C\times_kC\times_kC$ is open in $G\times_kG\times_kG$. The product $C\times_k C$ is irreducible by lem-sc-irreducible-product-over-field, since both factors are geometrically irreducible by step 3. It is therefore connected, and its multiplication image in $G$ is connected and contains $e$ (the image of $(e,e)$). It lies in $C$ by maximality of the connected component. Inversion also has connected image on $C$ and fixes $e$, so its image lies in $C$. Here continuous images preserve connectedness because a clopen separation of an image pulls back to a clopen separation of the source. The unit has image $e\in C$. Apply lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme to these three maps to obtain multiplication, inversion and unit on $C$. They satisfy the group diagrams: composing either side of each diagram with $C\hookrightarrow G$ gives the corresponding group diagram of $G$; uniqueness of factorization through the open immersion makes the original sides equal. Thus $C$ is an open subgroup scheme and its inclusion is a homomorphism. This uses the open scheme structure, not the reduction.

source.place: Tag 0B7R, proof: factor the unit, inversion and multiplication; use the open-immersion factorization instead of the general flat closed-immersion criterion.

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-irreducible-group-quasi-compact to the group scheme $C$ of step 4, irreducible by step 3. Hence $C$ is quasi-compact. It is locally of finite type over $k$: for any $c\in C$, take an affine finite-type chart $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq G$ containing $c$; principal affine opens are a basis, so some $D(f)$ contains $c$ and lies in $C\cap\operatorname{Spec}A$. Its algebra $A_f$ is generated over $k$ by finite generators of $A$ together with $f^{-1}$. These charts cover $C$ and quasi-compactness gives a finite subcover. By def-weil-finite-type-morphism this is finite type over $k$.

source.place: Tag 0B7P (lemma-irreducible-group-scheme-over-field-qc); Tag 0B7R, part (4); Morphisms Tag 01T0 (finite type).

proof.text: Fix any field extension $K/k$ and let $p:G_K\to G$ be its projection. By lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change, the pullback of $C\hookrightarrow G$ is an open immersion, and by lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product (with $U=V=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $W=C$) its image is $p^{-1}(C)$; likewise the pullback of the complementary open $G\setminus C$ has image $p^{-1}(G\setminus C)$. These complementary inverse images give a clopen decomposition of $G_K$, with the pullback open-subscheme structures. Geometric irreducibility of $C$ says that $C_K$ is nonempty and irreducible, hence connected. The base-changed unit factors through $C_K$ by the fibre-product definition of base change. Thus $C_K$ lies in the connected component of $e_K$ in $G_K$. Conversely this component cannot meet both pieces of the clopen decomposition and contains $e_K\in C_K$, so it lies in $C_K$. Their underlying subsets are equal. The component is therefore open, and both scheme structures are the restriction of $\mathcal O_{G_K}$ to this same subset. This proves $(G^0)_K=(G_K)^0$ as open subschemes, for every extension $K/k$.

source.place: Tag 0B7R, geometric irreducibility, with the clopen characterization; Schemes Tag 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion).
